title: Wholesale Credit, Always On
gist: BCG argues wholesale banks' credit bottleneck is the handoff-heavy operating model, and agentic AI can turn credit into an always-on, event-driven capability—cutting time to decision 40-60% and flagging 80-90% of deteriorating credits early. Success requires a shared agent ecosystem, a data ontology, deterministic math and provenance controls, with humans moving 'above the loop'.

themes.theme: Operating model, not tooling, is the credit bottleneck

insights.claim: BCG argues wholesale bank credit processes remain largely manual and sequential despite years of digitizing individual steps, with analysts acting as the connective tissue between systems, so better point tools yield only incremental gains.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Bank tech vendors selling point solutions face limited upside; value accrues to platforms that redesign end-to-end credit workflow.
insights.quote: As long as people remain the connective tissue between otherwise capable systems, much of the potential benefit remains out of reach.
insights.locator: The Constraint Is the Process

insights.claim: BCG identifies four reinforcing frictions in wholesale credit: a linear process where delays cascade and completed work goes stale, unit costs that rise with deal variability, an episodic request- or renewal-triggered cadence that leaves monitoring reactive, and data friction across email, spreadsheets and core systems—while regulatory documentation and traceability expectations keep rising.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Framework for diagnosing which banks have the most latent efficiency to unlock from agentic redesign.
insights.locator: Several sources of friction reinforce

insights.claim: BCG project experience indicates banks that redesign wholesale credit with agentic AI can cut time to decision by 40% to 60% versus traditional automation, especially for mid-market and large corporate clients.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Faster credit decisions can win share in competitive corporate lending; watch banks reporting cycle-time cuts.
insights.locator: The potential impact is significant

insights.claim: BCG describes agentic credit as turning a queued sequence into an always-on standing capability: new financial statements, covenant data, rating changes or payment deterioration automatically refresh only the dependent parts of the credit file, so most work is done before a client request arrives.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Shifts credit from episodic to continuous—a structural change in how banks manage portfolio risk and respond to clients.
insights.locator: From a Sequence to a Standing Capability

insights.claim: BCG argues agentic credit moves the credit officer from inside the loop (collecting, reconciling, moving files) to above the loop (reviewing, challenging exceptions and applying judgment), without removing humans from decisions.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Expect wholesale risk headcount mix to shift from assemblers toward fewer, higher-judgment reviewers.
insights.quote: The credit officer moves above the loop, reviewing what the system has assembled, challenging exceptions, and applying judgment where it is needed.
insights.locator: That changes the role of the credit officer

themes.theme: Value pools: capacity, speed, earlier intervention

insights.claim: BCG says improvements to the underlying credit platform and data alone can raise the share of applications processed without manual intervention by 10 to 20 percentage points, before agentic redesign adds further automation.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Data/platform modernization is the first-order lever; agentic gains build on it.
insights.locator: What It Is Worth, and to Whom

insights.claim: Where wholesale credit processes are redesigned rather than merely accelerated, BCG estimates risk and operations capacity requirements can fall 40% to 50% and relationship managers can recover 30% to 40% of their time for client coverage, though most banks redeploy rather than cut that capacity.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Efficiency gains likely show up as revenue-per-RM and coverage rather than headline cost cuts at banks.
insights.locator: Released Capacity

insights.claim: BCG argues that for a chief risk officer the most consequential benefit of agentic credit is not cost but continuous event-driven monitoring, which can identify 80% to 90% of deteriorating credits early enough to act, with 30% to 50% of those restructurable while still in Stage 2 before impairment.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Earlier intervention could reduce provisions and credit-loss volatility for adopting banks—relevant to bank credit-cost forecasts.
insights.quote: For the CRO, a more consequential benefit may be a shift from periodic review toward continuous, event-driven monitoring.
insights.locator: Earlier Risk Intervention

insights.claim: BCG estimates 50% to 60% of annual credit reviews can be closed quickly under agentic monitoring when nothing material has changed, letting analysts focus on exceptions, and a consolidated per-borrower exposure view lets banks manage limits at origination rather than correcting excesses later.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Large chunk of routine review work is automatable—a clear productivity lever for wholesale banks.
insights.locator: Earlier Risk Intervention

insights.claim: BCG argues SME lending offers more automation scope because applications are standardized, while large corporate credit is bespoke, yet lower automation in large corporate does not mean lower value because exposures are larger, slow responses cost more commercially, and missed risks show up as credit losses and provisions.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Don't judge AI value in banking by automation rate alone; large-corporate books may yield the biggest loss-avoidance payoff.
insights.locator: The degree of automation will vary

insights.claim: BCG notes speed is commercially important in wholesale banking because a shorter time to decision wins mandates when a client is comparing financing options or working against a transaction timetable.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Agentic credit adopters could gain share in corporate lending and deal financing.
insights.locator: Faster Client Response

themes.theme: Shared agent ecosystem over isolated pilots

insights.claim: BCG warns a common mistake is treating agentic credit as a single application such as a credit-memo drafting tool, when the opportunity spans the whole exposure life cycle—qualifying, assessing, drafting, policy validation, booking, monitoring and responding to change.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Narrow 'memo copilot' products may be commoditized; value lies in platforms spanning the credit life cycle.
insights.locator: Build an Ecosystem, Not a Product

insights.claim: BCG argues reusable agent capabilities—reading statutory accounts, normalizing data and producing ratios, external data retrieval, document processing, peer benchmarking, narrative drafting—serve both origination and monitoring, and reuse is central to the economics, requiring shared guardrails, audit trails, model life-cycle management and a common data ontology.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Banks that build shared foundations get compounding returns on each new agent; isolated pilots duplicate costs.
insights.locator: Those are separate solutions, with different owners

insights.claim: One European wholesale bank has designed an ecosystem of 15 credit agents and is deploying them in waves, starting with four foundational agents that provide building blocks for the rest.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Signals the realistic sequencing and scale of agentic deployment at leading banks.
insights.locator: Leading banks therefore design the target ecosystem

insights.claim: BCG recommends a single business case for wholesale lending rather than funding agent by agent, because shared foundations otherwise lack an owner—critical in a sector where more than 60% of bank technology spending typically goes to running the bank rather than changing it.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: With most bank IT budget locked in run costs, change budgets for AI are scarce—favor banks with consolidated transformation programs.
insights.locator: The same logic applies to the business case

themes.theme: Control design: deterministic math, provenance, human gates

insights.claim: BCG recommends that language models never compute numbers in credit memos: ratios, concentration percentages and limit totals should come from deterministic code, with agents only explaining and contextualizing them, to make outputs defensible to model-risk functions and supervisors.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Key regulatory-acceptance design principle; vendors violating it face supervisory pushback.
insights.quote: Don’t let language models compute numbers.
insights.locator: Three design principles are especially important

insights.claim: BCG argues the agentic layer should orchestrate a bank's existing validated deterministic tools—rating models, pricing engines, limit systems, scoring models and stress grids—rather than replacing them.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Incumbent core risk systems remain sticky; agentic AI is complementary, not a displacement threat, to risk-infrastructure vendors.
insights.quote: the agentic layer orchestrates existing risk infrastructure rather than replacing it
insights.locator: Use the bank’s existing deterministic layer

insights.claim: BCG describes a two-subsystem credit memo design working from one shared record of facts: one compiles a client knowledge base where every fact carries its source, read date and producer (an unsupported number is a defect), and another challenges the output against bank rules with deterministic checks plus a citation-bound agent, with a human reviewing each finding.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Provenance and traceability will be prerequisites for regulated AI deployment in lending.
insights.quote: A number that appears in the memo without a supporting fact is treated as a defect.
insights.locator: Inside a Solution: One System Writes

insights.claim: BCG recommends banks reduce human oversight of agentic credit only progressively and where evidence supports it, noting the point at which the human gate can safely be removed will differ between SME and large corporate credit.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Expect automation to advance first in SME books; large corporate will keep human gates longer.
insights.locator: Reduce human oversight only when warranted

insights.claim: Per a BCG study, only 5% of companies are achieving AI value at scale while 60% are not yet generating material value from AI investments.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Most enterprise AI spend is not yet paying off—be skeptical of broad AI ROI claims; dispersion between leaders and laggards is extreme.
insights.locator: What It Takes

insights.claim: BCG's rule of thumb is that roughly 10% of AI transformation effort should go to algorithms, 20% to technology and data, and 70% to people and processes, which for banks means investing in the 'harness engineering' of governance, controls, context and operating structures around models.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Advantage in banking AI accrues to execution and process redesign, not model access—model quality is not the moat.
insights.locator: What It Takes

insights.claim: BCG argues banks must invest in a data ontology mapping how clients, contracts, ratings and covenants relate before building agents, and must curate gold-standard credit memos and a proprietary knowledge base that cannot be bought off the shelf because it encodes the bank's own judgment.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Proprietary institutional knowledge is a durable differentiator; off-the-shelf AI vendors can't supply it.
insights.quote: This pool of knowledge cannot be bought off the shelf because it encodes the bank’s own judgment.
insights.locator: Define the standards and knowledge base

insights.claim: BCG concludes that the banks moving fastest in agentic credit are not those with the most advanced models but those treating it primarily as process redesign with AI as an enabler and credit professionals at the center.
insights.speaker: Stiene Riemer
insights.so_what: Pick bank winners on operating-model change, not AI announcements or model partnerships.
insights.quote: The banks moving fastest in agentic credit are not necessarily those with the most advanced models.
insights.locator: The banks moving fastest in agentic credit
